chapters.title: Run and export reports
chapters.subtitle: Find a report, set its period and filters, and take it away as a file

steps.text: Reports show what happened in your contact center and your C.R.M. over a period you choose. This video shows how to find a report, set its date range and filters, and export it to CSV, Excel or PDF.

chapters.title: Why reports
chapters.subtitle: A question about work that already happened

steps.text: A report answers a question about work that already happened: how many calls came in, how many were answered, and which campaign turned leads into customers.
Every number is worked out from your records when you open the report, so it always matches what you picked: the period, the queue, the agent.
You read the figures on screen, or take them away as a file for a spreadsheet, a meeting or an archive.

chapters.title: Find a report
chapters.subtitle: The Reports menu and the Reports page

steps.text: Every report lives under Reports in the admin menu. They are grouped by category: Operations, Agent Performance, Queue and Routing, Workforce and Payroll, CRM and Campaigns, and more.
Reports itself opens the Reports page: one card for each report you may open, with a line that says what it answers.
Click a card, or pick the report from the menu. Here it is Call insights, under Operations.

Which reports you see depends on your role. Under Roles, search the permissions for reports. View Contact Center reports opens the Contact Center reports, and View Omnichannel reports opens the CRM and campaign reports.
Another report can bring a permission of its own, such as Run Phone Number Verifications Report. Give a role only the ones its members need.
This is the Reports page of a user whose role has only View Contact Center reports. The Contact Center reports are listed; the CRM reports, such as Lead funnel, are not.
The top of every report is its filter bar. The first filter is the Date range, and its button states the range in words.
Click it to choose. Relative days run from Today to Last 90 Days. Calendar periods cover this week, this month, this quarter and this year, and the ones before them.
Rolling months cover the last three, six or twelve months. Custom Range takes a start and an end, and On or before and On or after leave one end open.
Pick Last 30 Days, and click Show. The report runs again for that period.
The summary shows the totals as cards: total calls, inbound and outbound, answered, abandoned, voicemail, callback requests, failures, average handle time and average speed of answer.
Below, the same calls are broken down by channel, by outcome and by day, so one page answers the first questions and points to where to look next.

chapters.title: Filters
chapters.subtitle: Narrow a report to what you want to see

steps.text: Each report offers the filters that make sense for it. Call insights offers Queue group, Queue, Agent, Direction and Channel.
A filter left on All does not narrow the report. Pick the Support queue and the Inbound direction, and click Show.
Every number is worked out again from the matching records: the cards, the breakdowns and the daily volume now describe only inbound calls to Support.
Other reports have other filters. Dialer call detail filters by campaign, source, status and disposition.
In Disposition you can tick several dispositions at once, to list the numbers that ended either way.
The Export menu sits above the report. With the Excel and PDF features on, it offers Export CSV, Export Excel and Export PDF. With only the Reports feature, it is a single Export CSV button.
An export uses the same date range and filters as the report on screen, and keeps the detail rows, subtotals and grand totals in the order shown. Export CSV downloads a plain file.
Export Excel puts each section of the report on its own worksheet.
Export PDF lays the report out as it looks on screen, with its charts, and numbers the pages.
This is the start of the CSV file the browser just saved. Its name holds the report and the first and last day of the period, and it opens in any spreadsheet.
The Excel workbook has one worksheet for each section of the report: the summary, and the breakdowns by channel, by outcome and by day.
And this is the first page of the PDF: the report as it looks on screen.

chapters.title: Long periods and missing features
chapters.subtitle: What a report says when it cannot answer

steps.text: Reports on agents' time read every state change of every agent, so they cover 31 days at a time. Pick Last 90 Days on Agent time summary, and click Show.
The report says the period is too long, and names the longest period it allows, instead of showing partial figures. Pick Last 30 Days, and the figures return.

A report that measures work from a feature your site does not use shows a notice naming that feature, instead of zeroes. Here the Contact Center Call Recording feature is off, and Recording coverage says so.
A weekly service review: open Queue service level for Last Week, filter by queue group, and read where calls waited too long.
A figure for someone else: export Excel for a finance team that wants rows, or PDF for a manager who wants the page.
Reports can also be emailed on a schedule, shown as tiles on a dashboard, and built from scratch with the Report Builder. Those have their own videos.
Reports turn the history of your contact center and your C.R.M. into figures you can filter and take away. Thanks for watching.
